image_description: A large, dark brown bison is lying down (recumbent) on a grassy slope next to a light-colored rock. The bison's head is turned slightly away from the camera, resting near its body. The forequarters are covered in thick, shaggy fur, while the hindquarters appear smoother. A second bison is partially visible in the background, mostly out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is visible but turned away and partially obscured by the angle and fur. Horns are not clearly distinguishable due to the recumbent pose and image resolution/angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The chin and throat area are pressed against the body or ground due to the lying-down pose, making this feature impossible to verify visually.
One eye is visible and appears dark, consistent with the species.
Ears are small and largely blended into the thick fur of the head, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The 'tall' proportion at the withers is a standing characteristic. Since the bison is lying down, the vertical height cannot be assessed accurately.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The forequarters show dense, shaggy dark brown fur. The shoulder hump is structurally present, though less pronounced than in a standing pose due to gravity and posture.
The visible rear section of the bison shows shorter, smoother hair compared to the front, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Horns are not clearly visible enough to judge their length relative to the body.
The legs are tucked underneath the body or obscured by the grass and rocks; hooves are completely invisible.
The tail is not visible in this frame/pose.
